general_hunter.title: Per-purchase price rounding lets buyers materially underpay by splitting purchases
general_hunter.description: The payment amount is calculated as floor(_amount * discountedPrice / 10**vestingTokenDecimals) independently for every purchase. There is no accumulation of the fractional remainder across purchases, so a buyer can split a listing into many purchases and repeatedly discard the fractional component. This violates the intended price-per-unit calculation and also reduces fee amounts because buyerFeeTotal and sellerFeeTotal are calculated from the rounded-down baseAmount.
general_hunter.impact: A public listing can be fully consumed for substantially less than its configured price. For example, with a 6-decimal vesting token, total=19,900, pricePerUnit=10,000, no discount, and minPurchaseAmt=100, a full purchase costs floor(19,900*10,000/1,000,000)=199 payment units. A buyer can instead make 100 purchases of 199 units; each costs floor(199*10,000/1,000,000)=1, so the entire listing costs only 100 payment units. The seller and fee collector lose the difference.
exploit_steps: A seller creates a public PARTIAL listing with a 6-decimal vesting plan, total amount 19,900 units, pricePerUnit 10,000, no discount, and minPurchaseAmt 100.
The buyer calls spotPurchase 100 times, purchasing 199 vesting units per call. Each amount satisfies the minimum and leaves the listing active until the final purchase.
For every call, _handleTransfers computes baseAmount as floor(199 * 10,000 / 1,000,000) = 1 payment unit.
After the 100th call, the buyer has received all 19,900 vesting units while paying only 100 payment units, instead of the 199 payment units charged by one full purchase.

general_hunter.title: Duplicate token-owner mappings allow cross-issuer vesting theft
general_hunter.description: setTokenOwner only checks whether the supplied owner already has a token entry; it does not prevent the same token from being assigned to multiple owners. The deployer then authorizes createVesting and transferVesting solely by checking that the caller's mapped token equals the selected vesting contract's token. It never verifies that the caller is the selected vesting contract's immutable tokenIssuer. Because SecondSwap_StepVesting authorizes the vestingDeployer to perform these operations, a second owner of the same token can operate on another issuer's vesting plan. In the creation path, _createVesting pulls funds from the plan's tokenIssuer, not from the caller.
general_hunter.impact: If two owners are mapped to the same token, the second owner can create vesting allocations for itself that are funded from the first issuer's balance and allowance, or transfer existing unclaimed allocations from arbitrary beneficiaries in the first issuer's vesting plans. This can directly drain issuer ERC20 funds or steal vested allocations.
exploit_steps: The administrator calls setTokenOwner(T, issuerA), then calls setTokenOwner(T, attacker), which succeeds because attacker currently has no token mapping and no reverse uniqueness check exists.
issuerA deploys a StepVesting plan P for token T and approves P to pull T tokens.
The attacker calls SecondSwap_VestingDeployer.createVesting(attacker, amount, P). The deployer check passes because _tokenOwner[attacker] equals P.token().

The deployer calls P.createVesting; P accepts the deployer as an authorized caller and _createVesting executes token.safeTransferFrom(tokenIssuer, address(this), amount), pulling the amount from issuerA while crediting the attacker.

Alternatively, the attacker calls transferVesting(issuerA, attacker, amount, P, transactionId), causing the deployer to move issuerA's existing vesting allocation to the attacker because the arbitrary grantor is not restricted to the caller or P.tokenIssuer.
The attacker waits for or uses the vesting schedule to claim the stolen allocation, or lists/transfers it through the marketplace.

general_hunter.title: Uninitialized vesting-manager proxy allows theft of marketplace custody
general_hunter.description: The upgradeable vesting manager exposes an unrestricted initializer that only relies on the Initializable one-time guard. If the proxy is deployed without atomically invoking initialize, any account can become s2Admin. That account can set marketplace to an arbitrary address, and completePurchase only checks that msg.sender equals this mutable marketplace address before transferring allocations from address(this) to the supplied buyer.
general_hunter.impact: An attacker can take control of an uninitialized manager proxy, allow legitimate users to list vesting allocations into manager custody, then change marketplace to the attacker's address and drain those custody allocations without paying for them.
exploit_steps: Deploy the SecondSwap_VestingManager proxy without calling initialize in the same deployment transaction.
Call initialize(attacker) to set the attacker as s2Admin.
Call setMarketplace(actualMarketplace) so legitimate marketplace listings are accepted.
Have sellers list vesting allocations; the manager transfers those allocations to address(this).
Call setMarketplace(attacker) as the manager admin.

Call completePurchase(attacker, vestingPlan, amount) for the custody balance. The manager calls transferVesting(address(this), attacker, amount), transferring the listed allocations to the attacker without any payment.

general_hunter.title: Early-unlisting penalty uses 18-decimal wei units for an arbitrary ERC20
general_hunter.description: The default penaltyFee is initialized to 10 ether, and unlistVesting passes that value directly to the configured USDT token's balanceOf and safeTransferFrom. ERC20 amounts are denominated in the token's smallest units, but the code never normalizes the penalty by usdt.decimals(). For a normal 6-decimal USDT, 10 ether is 10^19 base units, equivalent to 10 trillion USDT rather than 10 USDT.
general_hunter.impact: Sellers cannot early-unlist unless they hold and approve an enormous token amount. If they do satisfy the check, the contract transfers the mis-scaled amount to the fee collector, materially overcharging the seller.
exploit_steps: Configure the settings contract with a standard 6-decimal USDT token.
Create a listing and attempt to unlist it before minListingDuration expires.
The marketplace requires balanceOf(msg.sender) >= 10^19 and then calls safeTransferFrom for 10^19 raw USDT units.
A seller holding the intended 10 USDT penalty fails the balance check and cannot early-unlist; a seller holding the required amount loses 10 trillion USDT units.

general_hunter.title: Uninitialized vesting deployer proxy permits arbitrary allocation transfers
general_hunter.description: The upgradeable vesting deployer exposes an unrestricted initializer and does not disable initialization on the implementation. If its proxy is deployed without atomically calling initialize, any account can set itself as s2Admin. The attacker can then register itself as an owner for an existing vesting token and call transferVesting. The deployer only checks _tokenOwner[msg.sender] against the selected vesting token, while the StepVesting contract authorizes the deployer address itself as vestingDeployer, allowing the attacker to transfer allocations out of plans created by the legitimate issuer.
general_hunter.impact: An attacker who initializes an uninitialized deployer proxy can steal arbitrary unclaimed allocations from existing vesting plans by transferring them to an address they control.
exploit_steps: Wait for the vesting deployer proxy to exist without having initialize called.
Call SecondSwap_VestingDeployer.initialize(attacker, configuredManager) from the attacker address.
Call setTokenOwner(targetToken, attacker) as the newly assigned s2Admin.
Call transferVesting(victim, attacker, amount, targetVesting, transactionId), where targetVesting was deployed through this deployer proxy and contains the victim's allocation.
The deployer authorization check passes because _tokenOwner[attacker] equals targetVesting.token(), and StepVesting authorization passes because msg.sender is the configured vestingDeployer proxy.

general_hunter.title: Uninitialized marketplace proxy allows settlement takeover
general_hunter.description: The upgradeable marketplace has a public initializer with no access restriction or validation of the settings address. If the proxy is not initialized atomically, the first caller can permanently set marketplaceSetting to an attacker-controlled implementation. All subsequent authorization, fee, vesting-manager, whitelist, and fee-collector decisions are obtained from that address.
general_hunter.impact: The attacker can permanently replace the marketplace's configuration, redirect fees, set arbitrary fee rates, or return a fake vesting manager that records listings without custody and completes purchases without transferring vesting allocations. Buyers can therefore pay for listings that deliver no vesting allocation.
exploit_steps: Deploy or identify a marketplace proxy that has not yet been initialized.
Deploy an attacker-controlled contract implementing IMarketplaceSetting, returning the attacker as s2Admin and feeCollector and returning an attacker-controlled vesting manager.
Call SecondSwap_Marketplace.initialize(paymentToken, maliciousSettings) before the legitimate deployer.
Use the malicious vesting manager's no-op listVesting, getVestingTokenAddress, and completePurchase implementations to create a listing for a fake vesting plan.

Induce a buyer to call spotPurchase on that listing; the marketplace transfers the buyer's payment to the attacker-controlled seller and feeCollector, then the no-op completePurchase leaves the buyer without the purchased allocation.

general_hunter.title: Fee-on-transfer payment tokens make seller payouts and marketplace solvency incorrect
general_hunter.description: addCoin enables any token selected by the admin without checking transfer semantics. During a purchase, _handleTransfers assumes that safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), baseAmount + buyerFeeTotal) credits the marketplace with the full requested amount, and then sends nominal amounts to the seller and feeCollector. Deflationary or fee-on-transfer ERC20s credit less than the requested amount, so the seller receives less than baseAmount - sellerFeeTotal, the feeCollector receives less than the recorded fee, or the transfers revert and purchases become unavailable.
general_hunter.impact: Purchases using a supported tax/deflationary token violate the payment invariant and can consume any pre-existing marketplace balance as subsidy. Depending on the token's transfer behavior, sellers and fee collectors are underpaid or all purchases using that currency are permanently blocked.
exploit_steps: Have the administrator add a fee-on-transfer ERC20 through addCoin.
Create a listing whose currency is that token and approve the marketplace for the buyer's nominal base amount plus buyer fee.
Call spotPurchase.
The token credits the marketplace with less than the requested amount, but the marketplace attempts to transfer the full nominal seller and fee amounts without checking its post-transfer balance.
Observe either a revert due to insufficient marketplace balance or a payout funded partly from the marketplace's existing token balance and reduced by the token's transfer fee.

general_hunter.title: Unbounded discounts can permanently make listings unpurchasable
general_hunter.description: listVesting only checks that a non-NO discount is greater than zero and never enforces discountPct <= BASE. Consequently, a FIX listing with discountPct == BASE produces a discounted price of zero and fails the later baseAmount > 0 check for every purchase, while a discountPct > BASE causes BASE - discountPct to underflow in _getDiscountedPrice. The listing itself is accepted and its vesting allocation is transferred into marketplace custody before any buyer attempts a purchase.
general_hunter.impact: A seller can create an active listing whose entire balance cannot be purchased. The allocation remains in marketplace custody until the seller unlists it, potentially requiring an early-unlisting penalty or administrative intervention.
exploit_steps: Obtain a sellable vesting allocation.
Call listVesting with DiscountType.FIX and discountPct equal to 10000 or greater than 10000.
The listing succeeds because the only discount validation is discountPct > 0, and the vesting allocation is moved into marketplace custody.
Have any buyer call spotPurchase for the listing. With discountPct == 10000, baseAmount is zero and _handleTransfers reverts; with discountPct > 10000, _getDiscountedPrice reverts due to underflow.
All purchases remain unavailable until the seller or administrator unlists the listing.

general_hunter.title: Fee-on-transfer vesting tokens leave allocations underfunded
general_hunter.description: Vesting creation records the full `_totalAmount` before calling `token.safeTransferFrom(tokenIssuer, address(this), _totalAmount)`, but never measures the vesting contract's actual balance increase. A fee-on-transfer token can therefore credit less than `_totalAmount` while the accounting still promises the full amount. Claims likewise account for and attempt to transfer the nominal amount without accounting for transfer fees.
general_hunter.impact: A vesting schedule can become permanently underfunded. For example, with a 10% transfer tax, creating a 100-token allocation records 100 while the contract receives only 90; the final claims revert once the contract balance is exhausted. If the token also taxes outgoing transfers, beneficiaries receive less than their recorded claim amounts.
exploit_steps: Deploy or select an ERC20 vesting token whose `transferFrom` deducts a fee while returning success.
Deploy a `SecondSwap_StepVesting` schedule for that token and approve it to pull the issuer's allocation.
Call `createVesting` for an amount such as 100 tokens; `_createVesting` records 100 but the vesting contract receives only the post-fee amount, such as 90.
Advance to the claimable period and have the beneficiary claim repeatedly.
After the available token balance is exhausted, the remaining nominal claim reverts permanently, or beneficiaries receive less than the recorded allocation if outgoing transfers are taxed.

general_hunter.title: Completed beneficiaries permanently lock all subsequent grants
general_hunter.description: When a beneficiary already has a vesting record and has claimed all vesting steps, `numOfSteps - _vestings[_beneficiary].stepsClaimed` equals zero. The existing-beneficiary branch avoids division by zero by setting `releaseRate = 0`, but it still increases `totalAmount` by the newly granted amount. Since `claimable()` computes `claimableSteps` from the same completed `stepsClaimed` value and then multiplies by the zero release rate, the new allocation can never become claimable.
general_hunter.impact: Any beneficiary who fully claims an allocation cannot receive another claimable grant in the same vesting contract. The newly funded allocation remains permanently locked unless a privileged actor transfers it elsewhere.
exploit_steps: Create a vesting allocation for a beneficiary.
Wait until all vesting steps are available and have the beneficiary call `claim()` so that `stepsClaimed == numOfSteps`.
Call `createVesting(beneficiary, newAmount)` through the token issuer, manager, or vesting deployer.
Observe that `_createVesting` increases `totalAmount` but sets `releaseRate` to zero.
Call `claim()` again after the vesting end time; `claimable()` returns zero because there are no remaining steps, so the new allocation cannot be claimed.

general_hunter.title: High-decimal vesting tokens make listings permanently unusable
general_hunter.description: The marketplace computes `10 ** IERC20Extended(...).decimals()` without bounding the returned decimal count. Although `listVesting` only checks that a `decimals()` call exists, an ERC20 returning a decimal count of 78 or more causes the exponentiation to overflow in Solidity 0.8 and revert. The same unchecked exponentiation exists in `_handleTransfers` for purchases.
general_hunter.impact: A vesting plan backed by a token with a sufficiently large `decimals()` value cannot be listed or purchased. The deployer accepts such tokens because it performs no decimal-range validation, leaving the plan's allocations unusable through the marketplace.
exploit_steps: Deploy or configure an ERC20 whose `decimals()` returns 78 or greater.
Deploy a `SecondSwap_StepVesting` plan using that token and make the plan sellable.
Call `listVesting` with a valid amount and price.
The preliminary `doesFunctionExist` check succeeds, but `10 ** decimals()` overflows at the base-price calculation and the listing reverts.
If a compatible listing or implementation reaches purchase pricing, `_handleTransfers` reverts for the same reason.

judged_findings.title: Partial vesting transfers inflate the grantor release rate
judged_findings.description: After subtracting a transferred amount from grantorVesting.totalAmount, transferVesting recalculates releaseRate as totalAmount / numOfSteps. It ignores amountClaimed and stepsClaimed, although claimable() uses the inflated rate for non-terminal claims without capping amountClaimed against totalAmount.
judged_findings.impact: A beneficiary who has already claimed vesting steps can transfer part of the remaining allocation and then claim more than the reduced allocation. The excess consumes tokens backing the transferred allocation and can leave buyers unable to claim.
exploit_steps: Create and fund a 10-step, 100-token allocation for Alice.
After five steps, Alice claims 50 tokens.
Alice transfers or lists 20 tokens. totalAmount becomes 80, amountClaimed remains 50, and releaseRate becomes 8 instead of the correct remaining-rate calculation.
After four more steps, Alice claims 32 tokens, increasing amountClaimed to 82 although totalAmount is only 80.
The two-token excess is taken from tokens backing the transferred allocation, causing the recipient's later claim to fail or be underfunded.

judged_findings.title: Invalid step duration breaks vesting timing and claims
judged_findings.description: The deployer only checks startTime < endTime and steps > 0, while the vesting constructor computes stepDuration using floor division. A duration shorter than the step count produces stepDuration == 0, and a non-divisible duration makes currentStep reach or exceed numOfSteps before endTime. claimable() divides by stepDuration and does not cap currentStep to numOfSteps.
judged_findings.impact: Schedules with zero step duration permanently revert on claims, locking funded tokens. Non-divisible schedules can fully unlock early and can store stepsClaimed greater than numOfSteps, causing later grants and transfers to revert.
exploit_steps: Deploy a schedule with a one-second duration and two steps; deployment succeeds and stepDuration is zero.
Create and fund an allocation, then call claim after startTime; claimable() reverts on elapsedTime / 0 on every attempt.
Alternatively deploy a five-second schedule with three steps; stepDuration is one second, so at T+3, before endTime, claimable() enters the terminal branch and releases the full allocation.
If claiming at the configured end time produces currentStep greater than numOfSteps, later additions to the beneficiary can revert on numOfSteps - stepsClaimed.

judged_findings.title: Duplicate token-owner mappings permit cross-issuer vesting theft
judged_findings.description: setTokenOwner prevents an owner from being mapped twice but does not enforce uniqueness of the token mapping. createVesting and transferVesting authorize callers solely because their mapped token equals the target plan's token; they do not require the caller to be the plan's immutable tokenIssuer.
judged_findings.impact: An owner mapped to the same ERC20 as another issuer can create allocations for itself funded from the other issuer's approved balance or transfer existing allocations from the other issuer's plan.
exploit_steps: The administrator maps token T to issuer A and then maps the same token T to attacker B; both calls succeed.
A deploys a vesting plan for T and approves the plan to pull T.
B calls createVesting(B, amount, plan); the deployer check passes and the plan pulls the amount from its immutable tokenIssuer A.
Alternatively, B calls transferVesting(victim, B, amount, plan, id) and moves the victim's unclaimed allocation because the deployer accepts B's token mapping.

judged_findings.title: Authorized issuers can drain marketplace custody directly
judged_findings.description: StepVesting allows tokenIssuer and vestingDeployer to call transferVesting with any _grantor, including the vesting manager address. The transfer updates only StepVesting records and does not decrement the manager's sold accounting or marketplace listing balance.
judged_findings.impact: A token issuer or authorized deployer can move allocations escrowed for active marketplace listings without payment. The listing remains active but its custody allocation is removed, so subsequent purchases or unlisting operations fail.
exploit_steps: A seller lists an allocation, causing the manager to receive it under address(this) in the vesting plan.
The token issuer calls transferVesting(address(manager), attacker, amount) on the plan.
The authorization succeeds because msg.sender is tokenIssuer, and the manager's allocation is debited without any marketplace notification.
A buyer attempts to purchase or the seller attempts to unlist; the manager cannot transfer the missing custody amount and the listing remains unusable.

judged_findings.title: Administrator rotation leaves stale privileged control planes
judged_findings.description: MarketplaceSetting, VestingManager, and VestingDeployer each store an independent s2Admin. setS2Admin on MarketplaceSetting does not update the manager or deployer administrator, so the former administrator remains authorized to change manager/deployer control state after the apparent handover.
judged_findings.impact: A former administrator can redirect the vesting manager's marketplace authorization and invoke completePurchase directly, transferring marketplace-held allocations without a listing or payment. The former administrator can also replace the deployer manager or token-owner mappings.
exploit_steps: Deploy the system with administrator A controlling MarketplaceSetting and VestingManager.
A calls MarketplaceSetting.setS2Admin(B); VestingManager.s2Admin remains A.
A calls VestingManager.setMarketplace(A), which succeeds under the stale manager admin.

A calls completePurchase(attacker, plan, amount) from A; the onlyMarketplace check now passes and the manager transfers custody allocations to attacker without checking marketplace listing state or payment.

judged_findings.title: Marketplace custody merges incompatible vesting progress
judged_findings.description: All marketplace listings for a plan use the single beneficiary address(this). When that record already exists, _createVesting adds the incoming amount but retains the existing stepsClaimed and amountClaimed, ignoring the source progress passed by transferVesting. Purchases then copy the pooled progress into the buyer's record.
judged_findings.impact: A buyer can receive an allocation too early or too late depending on which listing initialized the pooled record. Source allocations with different claimed histories no longer retain their own vesting schedule.
exploit_steps: At step 0, seller A lists tokens, initializing manager custody with stepsClaimed == 0.
At step 5, seller B claims the first five steps of a separate allocation and lists the remaining tokens.
The manager merges B's tokens into the existing custody record and preserves stepsClaimed == 0.
A buyer purchases B's listing and receives a record initialized from custody progress 0, allowing claims for elapsed steps that B's transferred tranche had already passed.

judged_findings.title: Referral rewards are reported but never paid
judged_findings.description: For a public purchase with a referral, _handleTransfers computes referralFeeCost but performs no transfer to _referral or referralFeeCollector. It transfers the entire buyerFeeTotal plus sellerFeeTotal to feeCollector, while spotPurchase emits referralFeeCost as referralReward.
judged_findings.impact: Referrers receive no reward and the fee collector retains the referral portion. The Purchased event reports a reward that was not transferred; the reported value is also the buyer-fee remainder rather than the configured referral share.
exploit_steps: Configure a nonzero referralFee and create a public listing.
Have a buyer approve the payment token and call spotPurchase with a distinct nonzero referral address.
Observe that referralFeeCost is calculated and emitted, but no transfer reaches the referral address or referralFeeCollector.
Observe that the full buyer and seller fees are sent to feeCollector.

judged_findings.title: Changing the marketplace vesting manager strands existing listings
judged_findings.description: Listings transfer custody to the vesting manager configured at listing time, but the listing stores no manager address. Later unlist and purchase operations use the current MarketplaceSetting.vestingManager instead.
judged_findings.impact: After a manager rotation, existing listings remain recorded in the old marketplace and their allocations remain in the old manager, while the marketplace calls the new manager for settlement. Purchases and seller recovery revert until the old manager is restored.
exploit_steps: Configure manager M1 and create a listing, moving the allocation into M1 custody.
Call MarketplaceSetting.setManager(M2).
Attempt to purchase the old listing; the marketplace calls M2.completePurchase, which cannot transfer M1's custody allocation.
Attempt to unlist; the marketplace calls M2.unlistVesting and likewise fails, leaving the allocation stranded in M1.

judged_findings.title: Changing the manager marketplace strands old marketplace listings
judged_findings.description: onlyMarketplace accepts only the mutable marketplace address. setMarketplace replaces that address without preserving authorization for the old marketplace or migrating its listing records.
judged_findings.impact: Listings stored in the old marketplace remain active while their custody allocations are inaccessible through normal unlisting and purchase flows. The new marketplace has no records for the old listings.
exploit_steps: Configure the manager to accept Marketplace1 and create a listing through it.
Call VestingManager.setMarketplace(Marketplace2).
Have Marketplace1 call unlistVesting or completePurchase for the old listing; onlyMarketplace rejects the call.
Marketplace2 cannot recover the listing because its own listings mapping does not contain Marketplace1's records.

judged_findings.title: Rotating the vesting deployer leaves old plans authorized to the retired deployer
judged_findings.description: setVestingDeployer changes only the manager's configured deployer. Each StepVesting stores the deployer address supplied at construction and uses that stored address for authorization; existing plans have no migration path.
judged_findings.impact: A new deployer cannot create or transfer allocations in pre-rotation plans, while the retired deployer remains authorized to perform those operations indefinitely.
exploit_steps: Deploy a plan through deployer D1; the plan stores D1 as vestingDeployer.
Set the manager's vestingDeployer to D2.
D2 attempts createVesting or transferVesting on the old plan and is rejected by the plan's stored authorization.
D1 can still call those operations on the old plan despite no longer being the configured deployer.

judged_findings.title: Marketplace freeze blocks the only seller recovery path
judged_findings.description: unlistVesting is protected by isFreeze. The freeze check executes before the seller/admin authorization and manager unlisting call, so freezing also prevents recovery of allocations already held in custody.
judged_findings.impact: All active listings can remain locked for the freeze period. Neither sellers nor the administrator can close listings and recover their allocations while the marketplace is frozen.
exploit_steps: Create a listing so the manager takes custody of the seller's allocation.
Set marketplace freeze to true through MarketplaceSetting.
The seller calls unlistVesting and is rejected by isFreeze.
The administrator also calls unlistVesting and is rejected before the admin branch, leaving custody locked until unfreezing.

judged_findings.title: Sellability initialization conflates a valid zero cap with an uninitialized plan
judged_findings.description: setSellable uses maxSellPercent == 0 as an initialization sentinel. A token issuer may deliberately set maxSellPercent to zero, but a later setSellable(..., true) changes it to 2000 and resets fees to -1. Conversely, setting a nonzero cap before the first setSellable call skips initialization of buyerFee and sellerFee, leaving both at zero.
judged_findings.impact: A configured zero sale cap can be silently changed to a 20% cap, enabling sales the issuer prohibited. Plans preconfigured with a nonzero cap can also permanently bypass default buyer and seller fees.
exploit_steps: The token issuer calls setMaxSellPercent(plan, 0).
An authorized admin or deployer calls setSellable(plan, true); the manager writes maxSellPercent = 2000 and resets fees.
Sellers can now list within the restored 20% allowance.
Alternatively, set a nonzero maxSellPercent before the first setSellable call; the fees remain zero and purchases charge no default fees.

judged_findings.title: Self-purchases bypass the maximum sale percentage
judged_findings.description: _validatePurchase rejects a referral equal to msg.sender but never rejects msg.sender equal to listing.seller. completePurchase increments the seller's bought accounting while transferring the allocation back to that same seller.
judged_findings.impact: A seller can repeatedly self-purchase its own listings, increasing bought without obtaining any net allocation and thereby expanding the amount that the sale-limit calculation permits it to list for third-party buyers.
exploit_steps: Give seller S a 100-token allocation under a plan with a 20% max sale percentage.
S lists 20 tokens and calls spotPurchase on that listing as the buyer.
completePurchase increments allocations[S][plan].bought by 20 and transfers the 20 tokens back to S.
Repeat the cycle; the artificial bought amount increases the permitted sale allowance, allowing S eventually to list more than the configured cap to real buyers.

judged_findings.title: Clearing a vesting record resets its historical progress
judged_findings.description: A full transfer of an unclaimed record reduces totalAmount to zero but leaves stepsClaimed unchanged. The next _createVesting call treats totalAmount == 0 as a fresh record and overwrites stepsClaimed with the supplied value, normally zero.
judged_findings.impact: A beneficiary can receive a replacement allocation with vesting progress reset, making already elapsed steps claimable again and releasing newly funded tokens earlier than the schedule permits.
exploit_steps: Create an allocation for Alice and wait until several steps have elapsed without Alice claiming.
Transfer Alice's entire available allocation to another beneficiary; totalAmount becomes zero while stepsClaimed remains nonzero.
Create a new allocation for Alice.
The zero-total branch resets stepsClaimed to zero, allowing Alice to claim from step zero instead of continuing from her previous progress.

judged_findings.title: Late grants receive retroactive elapsed-step credit
judged_findings.description: createVesting always calls _createVesting with _stepsClaimed == 0 for a new beneficiary, regardless of the global schedule's elapsed time. claimable() then credits all current steps to that record.
judged_findings.impact: Allocations created after the schedule starts can be claimed immediately for steps that elapsed before the grant existed. Top-ups to an existing record are also recalculated over the remaining steps, allowing the new amount to participate in elapsed steps.
exploit_steps: Deploy a plan and wait until several global steps have elapsed.
Create a new allocation for a beneficiary through the deployer.
The beneficiary calls claim; currentStep is greater than zero while stepsClaimed is zero, so prior elapsed steps are released immediately.
Repeat with a top-up to an existing beneficiary to include the new amount in already elapsed claimable steps.

judged_findings.title: Allocations added after completion cannot be transferred to new beneficiaries
judged_findings.description: If a beneficiary's existing record has stepsClaimed == numOfSteps, a later createVesting call can add totalAmount while retaining that completed progress. Transferring the new available amount to a beneficiary with no record passes numOfSteps as _stepsClaimed and computes _totalAmount / (numOfSteps - _stepsClaimed), which divides by zero.
judged_findings.impact: New allocations added after a beneficiary completes the schedule can be claimable by the original beneficiary but cannot be transferred or listed through the marketplace.
exploit_steps: Create and fully claim Alice's original allocation so Alice.stepsClaimed == numOfSteps.
Create an additional allocation for Alice after completion; the existing-record branch adds it while retaining completed progress.
Alice attempts to list or transfer the new allocation to a fresh beneficiary.
_transferVesting reaches the fresh beneficiary branch with _stepsClaimed == numOfSteps and reverts on division by zero.

judged_findings.title: Small allocations are delayed until the terminal step
judged_findings.description: _createVesting calculates releaseRate using integer division. When an allocation is smaller than the remaining step count, releaseRate becomes zero, and non-terminal claimable amounts remain zero until the terminal branch returns the full remainder.
judged_findings.impact: Small allocations cannot be withdrawn during intermediate vesting periods and claim() reverts until the schedule reaches its terminal step, delaying access to the allocation for nearly the entire schedule.
exploit_steps: Deploy a valid schedule with at least 100 remaining steps.
Create an allocation of one raw token unit; releaseRate becomes zero.
At intermediate steps, call claimable or claim; the claimable amount is zero and claim reverts.
Only when the terminal condition is reached does claimable return the remaining token.

judged_findings.title: Out-of-range discounts create permanently unpurchasable listings
judged_findings.description: listVesting checks only that a non-NO discount is greater than zero and does not enforce discountPct <= BASE. A FIX discount of BASE produces discountedPrice == 0, while a larger discount underflows in BASE - discountPct.
judged_findings.impact: Sellers can transfer allocations into marketplace custody through listings that no buyer can purchase, requiring delisting or administrative recovery.
exploit_steps: Create a FIX listing with a positive amount and discountPct == 10000; listVesting accepts it using the undiscounted price.
A buyer calls spotPurchase; discountedPrice and baseAmount are zero, so the purchase reverts.
Alternatively use discountPct > 10000; purchase attempts revert during the subtraction underflow.

judged_findings.title: Fixed discounts truncate valid aggregate prices to zero
judged_findings.description: For FIX discounts, the contract first truncates the per-unit price as pricePerUnit * (BASE - discountPct) / BASE and only then multiplies by the purchase amount. Listing validation checks the undiscounted total and does not require the discounted unit price to be nonzero.
judged_findings.impact: A listing can have a mathematically positive aggregate discounted price but remain permanently unpurchasable because the truncated unit price is zero.
exploit_steps: Use a zero-decimal vesting token and list 10,000 units at pricePerUnit 1 with a FIX discount of 9999.
The listing passes because its undiscounted base amount is 10,000.
On full purchase, discountedPrice becomes zero and _handleTransfers reverts on baseAmount > 0.
The allocation remains in marketplace custody until delisting.

judged_findings.title: Linear discounts lose precision before price multiplication
judged_findings.description: The linear discount path computes (_amount * discountPct) / listing.total before multiplying by pricePerUnit. The fractional discount is therefore truncated before it is applied to the price.
judged_findings.impact: Buyers are overcharged whenever the proportional discount is less than one basis point after truncation; the discrepancy can be material for large prices and repeated partial purchases.
exploit_steps: Create a LINEAR listing with total 3e18, pricePerUnit 1e18, and discountPct 1.
Purchase 1e18 units.
The contract computes (1e18 * 1) / 3e18 == 0, applies no discount, and charges the full price instead of retaining the fractional discount.

judged_findings.title: Per-purchase price rounding lets buyers underpay by splitting fills
judged_findings.description: Each purchase independently floors (_amount * discountedPrice) / 10**decimals. Fractional payment remainders are discarded and never accumulated across fills.
judged_findings.impact: A buyer can consume a listing for less than its aggregate configured price, reducing both seller proceeds and fee revenue.
exploit_steps: Create a partial listing using a 6-decimal vesting token with total 19,900 units, pricePerUnit 10,000, and minimum purchase 100.
Purchase 199 units in 100 separate transactions.
Each purchase floors 199 * 10,000 / 1,000,000 to one payment unit, so the buyer pays 100 units total instead of the 199 units charged for one full purchase.

judged_findings.title: Per-purchase fee rounding allows fee avoidance
judged_findings.description: BuyerFeeTotal and sellerFeeTotal are rounded down independently for every purchase, with no remainder accumulation.
judged_findings.impact: A buyer can split a purchase into sufficiently small fills so each fee rounds to zero, depriving the fee collector and increasing seller proceeds relative to the configured aggregate fees.
exploit_steps: Create a partial listing where each one-unit purchase produces baseAmount 25 and buyer and seller fees are 250 basis points.
Purchase four units in four separate transactions.
Each fee calculation floors 25 * 250 / 10000 to zero, whereas one aggregate purchase would charge nonzero fees.

judged_findings.title: Fixed-discount multiplication can overflow after listing acceptance
judged_findings.description: The FIX discount path multiplies pricePerUnit by BASE - discountPct before dividing by BASE. Listing creation validates amount * price but does not validate this later intermediate multiplication.
judged_findings.impact: A valid listing can be created whose purchases always revert during discount calculation, leaving its allocation in marketplace custody.
exploit_steps: Use a zero-decimal vesting token and a one-unit listing.
Choose pricePerUnit slightly above type(uint256).max / 10000 and discountPct == 1.
The listing's undiscounted amount is representable and positive, so listing succeeds.
A buyer attempts to purchase and the pricePerUnit * 9999 multiplication overflows.

judged_findings.title: Linear-discount multiplication can overflow during purchase
judged_findings.description: The linear pricing branch evaluates _amount * listing.discountPct in checked arithmetic. Listing creation never evaluates or bounds this product.
judged_findings.impact: A listing can be accepted but become unpurchasable for a full or large partial fill when the amount-times-discount intermediate overflows.
exploit_steps: Create a zero-decimal listing with amount 2^244, pricePerUnit 1, and a valid linear discount of 5000.
The listing succeeds because amount * pricePerUnit fits and the linear formula is not evaluated at listing time.
Attempt to purchase the full balance; amount * 5000 overflows and the purchase reverts.

judged_findings.title: Fee multiplication overflow locks large purchases
judged_findings.description: Fee calculations multiply the entire baseAmount by the basis-point fee before dividing by BASE. The intermediate product can overflow even when the final fee and total payment would fit.
judged_findings.impact: Large but otherwise valid listings become unpurchasable and remain in custody. With the default 250-basis-point fee, baseAmount values above max / 250 trigger the overflow.
exploit_steps: Use a zero-decimal vesting token and create a one-unit listing with a price producing a baseAmount greater than max / 250 but well below max.
Ensure the listing uses the default buyer fee and the buyer has sufficient funds.
Call spotPurchase; buyerFeeTotal = baseAmount * 250 / BASE reverts before settlement.

judged_findings.title: Referral accounting has an additional overflow path
judged_findings.description: When a referral is supplied, the contract evaluates baseAmount * bfee * referralFee in checked arithmetic even though buyerFeeTotal was already divided by BASE and the resulting payment may fit.
judged_findings.impact: Large purchases can succeed without a referral but selectively revert whenever a referral address is provided.
exploit_steps: Configure a plan-specific buyer fee of 1 basis point and a nonzero referral fee such as 1000 basis points.
Create a listing with baseAmount near type(uint256).max / 2.
Purchase without a referral to show the base payment and buyer fee fit.
Repeat with a referral address; baseAmount * 1 * 1000 overflows and the purchase reverts.

judged_findings.title: Buyer fee addition can overflow valid payments
judged_findings.description: The marketplace computes baseAmount + buyerFeeTotal without checking the addition. Both values and the fee multiplication can individually fit while their sum exceeds uint256.
judged_findings.impact: Near-maximum-price listings cannot be purchased even though the base amount and fee are individually representable.
exploit_steps: Use a zero-decimal vesting token and configure a 1-basis-point buyer fee.
List one unit at pricePerUnit = type(uint256).max - 1.
The base amount and buyer fee calculation fit, but adding the positive fee to the near-maximum base amount overflows and reverts.

judged_findings.title: Sale-limit multiplication can overflow before division
judged_findings.description: listVesting calculates the additional allowance as (allocation * maxSellPercent) / BASE, multiplying before dividing. Solidity checked arithmetic reverts when the qualifying allocation exceeds max / maxSellPercent even though the final percentage result would fit.
judged_findings.impact: Very large but otherwise valid allocations cannot be listed.
exploit_steps: Create a sellable plan with an allocation greater than type(uint256).max / 2000 and the default 2000-basis-point cap.
Attempt to list any positive amount.
The manager's allocation * 2000 multiplication overflows before division and the listing reverts.

judged_findings.title: Listing value multiplication can overflow before decimal normalization
judged_findings.description: listVesting evaluates _amount * _price before dividing by 10**decimals. It does not use overflow-safe multiplication even when the normalized payment amount would fit.
judged_findings.impact: Large allocations with representable normalized prices cannot be listed.
exploit_steps: Use an 18-decimal vesting token and an allocation of at least 2^200 raw units.
Call listVesting with amount 2^200 and price 2^60.
The normalized result would fit, but the raw multiplication overflows and the listing reverts.

judged_findings.title: Vesting tokens with excessive decimals disable marketplace use
judged_findings.description: The marketplace computes 10 ** decimals() without bounding the returned uint8. Exponents of 78 or more overflow uint256. The deployer and listing path do not reject such tokens.
judged_findings.impact: Plans using a token that reports 78 or more decimals cannot be listed, and any purchase path reaching the same calculation reverts.
exploit_steps: Deploy or select an ERC20 whose decimals() returns 78 or greater.
Deploy a vesting plan and fund an allocation.
Call listVesting with otherwise valid parameters; the decimals existence check succeeds but 10 ** decimals overflows.
Any compatible purchase path reaches the same overflowing exponent.

judged_findings.title: Mutable vesting-token decimals change existing listing prices
judged_findings.description: listVesting reads the vesting token's decimals when validating the listing, while _handleTransfers reads decimals again at purchase time. The value is not snapshotted.
judged_findings.impact: A token administrator able to change decimals can make an existing listing charge materially more or less than the price accepted at listing time.
exploit_steps: Use a token whose decimals initially returns 6 and later changes to 18.
List an allocation at a price that produces the expected six-decimal payment.
Change the token's decimals to 18 before purchase.
The purchase recalculates the payment using 10**18, materially changing the required amount.

judged_findings.title: Early-unlisting penalty is mis-scaled for standard USDT
judged_findings.description: The default penaltyFee is initialized as 10 ether, an 18-decimal value, and is passed directly to a token described as USDT without converting for that token's decimals.
judged_findings.impact: With six-decimal USDT, the default penalty requires 10^19 raw units, equal to 10^13 USDT, so ordinary sellers cannot early-unlist and recover their custody allocation.
exploit_steps: Deploy settings with a standard six-decimal USDT and leave penaltyFee at 10 ether.
Create a listing and attempt seller unlisting before minListingDuration expires.
The balance check requires 10^19 raw USDT units and reverts for a normal seller.
The allocation remains in custody until the duration expires or an administrator intervenes.

judged_findings.title: Live duration and penalty settings can change existing unlisting terms
judged_findings.description: Listing stores listTime but does not snapshot minListingDuration or penaltyFee. unlistVesting reads both values from current settings when the seller exits.
judged_findings.impact: An administrator can increase the required waiting period or penalty for already-created listings, preventing sellers from recovering allocations under the terms in effect when they listed.
exploit_steps: Create a listing while the duration is 120 seconds and penalty is 10 USDT.
Before the original duration expires, increase the duration and penalty in settings.
The seller attempts to unlist the original listing.
The marketplace applies the new duration and penalty, potentially making the seller unable to recover the allocation.

judged_findings.title: Live fee settings alter already-created listings
judged_findings.description: Listing does not store buyerFee or sellerFee. spotPurchase calls _getFees at execution time and reads current plan-specific or marketplace-wide settings.
judged_findings.impact: Administrators or plan administrators can change the fees applied to active listings, increasing buyer costs or reducing seller proceeds after the seller committed to the listing.
exploit_steps: Create a listing while buyer and seller fees are 250 basis points.
Before purchase, change the applicable seller fee to 5000 basis points.
A buyer purchases the existing listing.
spotPurchase reads the new fee and pays the seller only baseAmount minus the newly configured fee.

judged_findings.title: Maximum listing duration can block seller delisting
judged_findings.description: setMinListingDuration accepts any nonzero uint256. Seller unlisting evaluates listing.listTime + minListingDuration using checked arithmetic.
judged_findings.impact: Setting the duration to type(uint256).max causes the addition to overflow for listings created at nonzero timestamps, preventing sellers from unlisting until the administrator changes the setting.
exploit_steps: The administrator sets minListingDuration to type(uint256).max.
A seller creates a listing at a normal nonzero timestamp.
The seller calls unlistVesting before administrative intervention.
The deadline addition overflows and the unlisting reverts.

judged_findings.title: Partial listings accept impossible minimum purchase amounts
judged_findings.description: The listing-time validation bounds minPurchaseAmt only for SINGLE listings. For PARTIAL listings it can exceed the entire listing balance, while purchase validation requires amount >= minPurchaseAmt unless amount == balance.
judged_findings.impact: A partial listing with minPurchaseAmt greater than total can never be purchased and keeps the allocation in custody until delisting.
exploit_steps: Create a PARTIAL listing for 100 units with minPurchaseAmt 101.
The listing succeeds because the SINGLE-only validation is skipped.
Attempt purchases from 1 through 100; every amount is below minPurchaseAmt and none equals a balance greater than 100.
All purchases revert and the listing remains active.

judged_findings.title: Small allocations can be blocked by sale-percentage truncation
judged_findings.description: The additional sale allowance uses integer division. With the default 20% cap, an allocation of one raw unit produces a zero allowance.
judged_findings.impact: Holders of small positive allocations cannot list any amount even though the plan is sellable and its configured percentage is positive.
exploit_steps: Create a one-unit allocation with no bought or sold accounting.
Call listVesting for one unit using a price that produces a positive payment amount.
The manager computes floor(1 * 2000 / 10000) == 0, increments sold to one, and reverts because sold exceeds the zero limit.

judged_findings.title: Zero-address payment tokens create unusable listings
judged_findings.description: initialize and addCoin accept address(0) as a supported payment currency. listVesting accepts a listing using that currency, but settlement calls SafeERC20 transfer functions on the non-token address.
judged_findings.impact: Listings using the zero payment token cannot be settled and leave the seller's allocation in marketplace custody until administrative or seller delisting.
exploit_steps: Initialize the marketplace with address(0) as the payment token or add address(0) through addCoin.
Create a valid listing using address(0) as currency; the support check passes and custody is transferred.
A buyer calls spotPurchase.
The payment-token SafeERC20 call to the zero address fails, so the listing cannot be purchased.

judged_findings.title: Zero USDT configuration blocks early seller recovery
judged_findings.description: The settings constructor accepts address(0) for _usdt. Early seller unlisting unconditionally calls balanceOf and safeTransferFrom on the configured USDT address.
judged_findings.impact: A marketplace deployed with a zero USDT address cannot execute seller-initiated early unlisting, leaving listed allocations inaccessible until the minimum duration expires or an administrator intervenes.
exploit_steps: Deploy MarketplaceSetting with _usdt == address(0).
Create a valid listing.
Before minListingDuration expires, call unlistVesting as the seller.
The balanceOf call on the zero address reverts before the manager returns the allocation.

judged_findings.title: Zero vesting-manager configuration disables marketplace operations
judged_findings.description: The settings constructor does not validate _vestingManager. Marketplace listing and settlement paths call the configured manager for token, listing, fee, and custody operations.
judged_findings.impact: A settings deployment with a zero vesting manager causes listing, purchasing, and other manager-dependent marketplace operations to revert.
exploit_steps: Deploy settings with vestingManager == address(0).
Configure the marketplace to use those settings.
Call listVesting with otherwise valid parameters.
The marketplace calls getVestingTokenAddress through the zero address and reverts; settlement paths are likewise unavailable.

judged_findings.title: Zero administrator values permanently disable privileged controls
judged_findings.description: The vesting manager and deployer accept address(0) during initialization and setAdmin without rejecting it. Their onlyAdmin modifiers require msg.sender == s2Admin.
judged_findings.impact: Once either administrator is set to address(0), all administrative configuration, recovery, and replacement operations for that contract become unreachable.
exploit_steps: Initialize the manager or deployer with a zero administrator, or have the current administrator call setAdmin(address(0)).
Attempt to call setAdmin or any other onlyAdmin function from a nonzero account.
The caller can never equal address(0), so privileged control remains permanently disabled.

judged_findings.title: Zero settings address permanently bricks the marketplace
judged_findings.description: Marketplace.initialize accepts address(0) for marketplaceSetting. isFreeze immediately calls isMarketplaceFreeze() on that address, while setMarketplaceSettingAddress first queries s2Admin() from the current settings address and therefore has no recovery path from the zero configuration.
judged_findings.impact: An accidentally or prematurely initialized marketplace cannot list, purchase, unlist, or replace its settings address.
exploit_steps: Call initialize with a valid or zero payment token and marketplaceSetting == address(0).
Attempt listVesting, spotPurchase, or unlistVesting; each reaches isFreeze and reverts when querying the zero settings address.
Attempt setMarketplaceSettingAddress with a valid settings contract; the authorization query to the zero current settings address also reverts.

judged_findings.title: Fee-on-transfer payment tokens break settlement accounting
judged_findings.description: The marketplace allows arbitrary payment tokens and assumes safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), nominalAmount) credits the full nominal amount. It then pays nominal seller and fee amounts without measuring the actual balance received.
judged_findings.impact: With a deflationary payment token, sellers or fee collectors can be underpaid, purchases can revert due to insufficient marketplace balance, or existing marketplace balances can subsidize the shortfall.
exploit_steps: Have the administrator add a fee-on-transfer ERC20 as a supported currency.
Create a listing using that token and approve the nominal payment amount.
Execute spotPurchase; the marketplace receives less than baseAmount plus buyer fees but attempts nominal transfers to the seller and fee collector.
Observe a revert or a payout funded partly by pre-existing marketplace balance.

judged_findings.title: Fee-on-transfer vesting tokens underfund recorded allocations
judged_findings.description: _createVesting records _totalAmount before calling token.safeTransferFrom(tokenIssuer, address(this), _totalAmount) and never checks the actual balance increase. Claims likewise account for nominal amounts without accounting for transfer taxes.
judged_findings.impact: A vesting record can promise more tokens than the contract received, causing final claims to revert or beneficiaries to receive less than the recorded claim amounts.
exploit_steps: Use a vesting token that deducts a transfer fee from transferFrom.
Create a 100-token allocation; the record stores 100 while the contract receives less.
Advance the schedule and claim repeatedly.
Once the actual balance is exhausted, remaining nominal claims revert or outgoing transfer fees reduce beneficiary receipts.

judged_findings.title: Changing the deployer's manager desynchronizes marketplace registration
judged_findings.description: VestingDeployer.setManager changes only the deployer's manager pointer. Newly deployed plans are registered as sellable in the new manager, while MarketplaceSetting.vestingManager can remain pointed to the old manager.
judged_findings.impact: New plans can be deployed and funded but cannot be listed because the marketplace queries the old manager, where the plan is not marked sellable.
exploit_steps: Configure manager A in MarketplaceSetting and in the deployer.
Configure manager B to accept the deployer, then call VestingDeployer.setManager(B) without changing MarketplaceSetting.
Deploy a new plan; B records it as sellable.
Attempt to list it through the marketplace; the marketplace asks manager A, sees sellable == false, and reverts.
